title: Priv EKS provisioner: 'seatbelt' Terraform module with automated health probes and upgrade hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a reusable Terraform module (seatbelt/priv-eks-provisioner) that will be the canonical path for provisioning Redwood Private EKS control planes. The module must be opinionated about safety: preflight validations, canary-style staged rollout, automated health probes, graceful drain/rollback hooks, and encrypted state integration with KMS. It should be suitable for both VPC-hosted and on-prem control-plane setups (where EKS APIs are proxied through our bootstrapper).

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: Terraform 1.6-compatible module, inputs for cluster control-plane config (subnets, kms_key_arn, control_plane_ami_override, version_channel), canary flags, health probe Lambda/agent orchestration, CloudWatch/DataDog metrics exporters, SSM parameter outputs, and upgrade lifecycle hooks (preflight, canary-promote, rollback).
- Out of scope: full Fleet orchestration (will be handled by follow-on orchestration layer), OS-image building pipeline, and on-host agent binary packaging (agents referenced as docker images from internal registry).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
1) Opinionated defaults: to reduce risky configuration drift the module will expose a small set of required variables and many vetted optional flags. This reduces flexibility but increases safety for most customers.
2) Health probe model: implement a two-part probe: (a) control-plane readiness prober (pod-level checks against kube-apiserver endpoints and ETCD snapshot succeed/latency), and (b) reconciliation watchdog (periodic sanity job that validates system-namespace controllers are progressing). The prober deploys as a Lambda (for hosted infra) or as a Kubernetes Job when bootstrapper access exists.
3) Upgrade strategy: support staged rollouts: preflight -> canary N nodes -> monitor (metric windows) -> promote/continue -> postflight validation. If metrics cross thresholds (error rate, API latency, pod eviction failure), an automated rollback plan is triggered with detailed diagnostics captured to S3.
4) State/backups: module will include optional automatic etcd snapshot configuration and integration with customer KMS for encrypted artifacts in S3.

Module inputs (high level):
- cluster_name (string)
- control_plane_subnet_ids (list)
- kms_key_arn (string)
- desired_k8s_version (string)
- canary_node_count (number)
- enable_autorepair (bool string)
- observability_backend (string: cloudwatch|datadog)
- preflight_prompt (string, optional link to eval criteria)

Module outputs (high level):
- control_plane_endpoint (string)
- management_role_arn (string)
- ssm_bootstrap_path (string)
- canary_status_s3 (string)

Observability and telemetry:
- Export metrics: api_latency_95, api_error_rate, node_drain_failures (CloudWatch namespace redwood/private-eks).
- Create dashboards and alerts: prebuilt DataDog dashboard JSON uploaded to docs repository; Terraform will register an alarm if api_error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m during upgrade windows.

Preflight checks implemented by module during apply (plan-time validations + optional pre-apply hook):
- CIDR/subnet overlap sanity check
- KMS key policy validation (module will fail if kms_key_arn is not usable by provisioning role)
- IAM role trust boundaries: ensure management role does not cross restricted account list when security_review_required=true
- Bootstrapper connectivity probe: attempt API handshake to provisioning orchestrator with configurable timeout

Upgrade/rollback behavior:
- Plan a dry-run step that creates a change-set artifact and uploads to S3.
- Canary: create canary control-plane node group(s) and shift a sample of traffic using header-based routing in the host proxy (we will provide helpers for gateway annotations).
- Monitor window: default 10 minutes (configurable). If any watch rule trips, automatically abort and run rollback playbook which: (1) drains canary nodes gracefully, (2) restore etcd from last healthy snapshot if etcd latency or snapshot failures observed, (3) open incident ticket template via GitHub Issues API.

Acceptance criteria / Done when:
- Terraform module published to internal module registry with semantic versioning and README + examples for VPC and on-prem flows.
- Automated unit tests for plan-time validations (using terratest or kitchen-terraform).
- End-to-end canary demo documented and validated in a staging account.
- Security review completed and e2e runbook created for ops.

Artifacts and links:
- PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2219
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/private-deploy/seatbelt-module/design.md
- Datadog dashboard template: https://drive.redwood.ai/dashboards/priv-eks-seatbelt.json
- Example terraform usage: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-examples/tree/main/priv-eks-seatbelt

Notes on uniqueness: This module intentionally packages a "seatbelt"—an opinionated minimal-surface Terraform module focused on safety-first defaults and automated health probes. It differs from prior modules by shipping both preflight plan-time validations and an action-oriented canary + rollback automation path tightly coupled to our observability signals, rather than relying on external orchestration entirely.

next_steps: Finish PR tests, schedule security follow-up, run full e2e upgrade canary in staging, publish module and update ops runbook
implementation_notes: Use terraform 1.6, provider aws v4.x. Prefer module layout: modules/seatbelt/{main.tf,variables.tf,outputs.tf,policy.tpl,tests/}. Use pre-apply hooks only for plan-time validations; runtime actions use synchronous lambda invocations recorded to S3.
qa_plan: 1) Run terratest suite in ephemeral staging account. 2) Execute canary upgrade with synthetic traffic generator. 3) Validate alarms fire and rollback completes. 4) Postmortem notes and checklist add to runbook.
owner_rotation: Oncall rotation will be added to 'private-deploy' pager duty after mainline merge
notes: Keep module surface intentionally small (<= 20 inputs) and expose advanced knobs via a 'advanced' map variable. Ensure all sensitive outputs are written to SSM with encryption and not printed in logs.
